title: An 85-to-230VAC to 3.3-to-4.6VDc 1.52W Capacitor-Drop Sigma-Floating-SC AC-DC Converter with 81.3% Peak Efficiency
problem: IoT and smart-home devices require high-efficiency, low-cost, compact non-isolated AC-DC converters for AC mains to battery-voltage output with large voltage conversion ratios (VCR). Traditional inductive switching converters are bulky; linear regulators are inefficient. Switched-capacitor approaches have poor output power scaling and lack voltage regulation.
motivation: Proliferation of intelligent IoT devices increases power consumption demands beyond passive capacitive rectifiers; non-isolated converters must achieve high efficiency while maintaining compact form factor and integrated circuit feasibility.
method: The device divides the high AC input voltage (85–230V) using a series stack of capacitors—a capacitor-drop topology that protects the internal converter stages. This sigma-floating switched-capacitor architecture uses a three-mode active rectifier (a circuit converting AC to DC with three distinct operating states) to adjust current flow, keeping the output voltage steady at 3.3–4.6V. Compared to earlier two-mode designs, the three-mode approach significantly reduces power wasted during idle periods.
key_novelty: This sigma-floating switched-capacitor architecture delivers regulated output power above 1 watt from AC mains with 81.3% efficiency, outperforming prior passive capacitor-based and hybrid switched-capacitor-linear-regulator designs.
contributions: Output power scaled to 1.52W (orders of magnitude higher than prior µW-level SC converters)
Regulated DC output (3.3-4.6VDc) without external trimming
Integrated on-chip solution reducing bulky external components
primary_theme: Sigma-floating switched-capacitor AC-DC converter for integrated IoT power delivery
